scope: RS3 Leagues II: Equilibrium research pass

pvme.coverage: All leaf links exposed by the current site navigation were attempted. This is navigation-complete, not a claim about unlinked/private URLs.

rsAnalysis.note: The homepage publication summary and authors were captured even though /research failed through the crawler.

policy.noCopy: Summaries are original project notes. No source code, UI, guide prose or calculator presentation is copied.
policy.dedupe: One normalized record per mechanic/dependency concept. Overlapping sources are merged into a single sources array.
policy.pvme: Discovery source by default. Re-verify values and changed mechanics against current Wiki/Jagex or another current explicit source before marking verified.
policy.rsAnalysis: Math/validation reference. Current exposed state/interactions may be explicit-source evidence; configured output numbers are not imported as universal base values.
policy.bossGuides: Boss-specific rotations, presets, phase guides, kill rates and enrage calculators are excluded.

records.summary: Treat damage as explicit state, not a single ability coefficient. The current calculators expose style level, hit chance/damage potential, hit-cap handling, target HP, prayer, vulnerability, Slayer-target modifiers and equipment/effect toggles separately.
records.leagueUse: Make these first-class inputs so relics and blessings can modify one layer without rewriting base ability data.

records.summary: A rotation needs timeline state: buffs, stacks, cooldowns, adrenaline, null/stall ticks, off-GCD actions, consumables, equipment swaps, familiars and poison all change later actions.
records.leagueUse: Use a tick timeline with state transitions. League effects enter as modifiers/events rather than special-case rotation code.

records.summary: The style calculators expose distinct state that should stay out of generic base damage.

ranged: Bow of the Last Guardian stacks

records.leagueUse: Store stacks, target geometry, temporary buffs and equipment-triggered effects independently so League modifiers can alter them without replacing ability records.

records.summary: Use Quantitative Analysis of RuneScape 3 Combat as a statistical-validation reference when its comparison or distribution concepts materially inform implementation.
records.leagueUse: Credit Akritia, Kyroh, Gamedolf and Sfox where their concepts/results are used. Do not copy prose, code, UI or presentation.

records.summary: RS Analysis currently lists perk-damage work for Aftershock, Crackling and Lunging as an active project, so its perk damage coverage is not treated as complete.
records.leagueUse: Keep perk damage behind a separate verification gate and prefer current Wiki/game-data confirmation before promoting values.

records.summary: PvME warns site-wide that most content predating the March 2, 2026 Combat Modernization is outdated.
records.leagueUse: Use PvME to discover mechanics, dependencies and interactions. Re-verify changed behaviour and values against current sources before promotion.

records.summary: Permanent combat progression spans abilities, Necromancy talents, Invention perks, potions, prayers, Archaeology relics, task-set rewards, quest unlocks, Livid Farm, War's Retreat, enchantments, animal perks and miscellaneous account unlocks.
records.leagueUse: Use these as planner checklist and region-value categories instead of reducing progression to a gear list.

records.summary: Quest dependencies worth joining to the region graph include combat ultimates, spellbooks, curses, Seren spells/prayers, Ancient Magicks additions, mobility/utility abilities and encounter access.
records.leagueUse: Join them to the existing quest-region graph, then let official League auto-completion remove prerequisites without inventing unlocks.

records.summary: Archaeology relics are a separate combat-progression layer with unlock requirements and a finite relic-energy budget.
records.leagueUse: Expose dig-site/relic access by region and treat relic energy as a constrained loadout resource separate from League relics.

records.summary: War's Retreat progression uses boss-kill/Marks of War milestones to unlock hub conveniences such as portals, combat facilities and campfire upgrades.
records.leagueUse: Track these as account unlock dependencies because League progression changes their practical value even when the underlying unlock remains unchanged.

records.summary: Invention power comes through augmentation, components, gizmos, perks, item levels and Ancient Invention. Perks occupy constrained weapon/armour gizmo slots and compete for those slots.
records.leagueUse: Map prerequisite skills, component sources and Ancient Invention by region. Store perk combinations and material requirements rather than a universal best-in-slot flag.

records.summary: PvME separates free/account unlocks from style purchases and the post-modernisation style pages use staged, content-dependent progression rather than one fixed endpoint.
records.leagueUse: Use the ordering as a dependency/priority candidate graph. Do not import live-game prices or assume the same priority under League drops, region locks and relics.

records.summary: Essence of Finality stores a weapon special attack and lets that attack be used through the amulet while other equipment is worn.
records.leagueUse: Model stored special attack separately from the equipped weapon and make the stored weapon an unlock/input.

records.summary: Queueing, stalling, target loss and late-adrenaline interactions can change when an action becomes legal or resolves. Rotation choice also depends on strength, cooldowns, weapon requirements, buff windows and scenario-specific DoT behaviour.
records.leagueUse: Keep these as optional timeline rules and action-scoring inputs, not base ability coefficients or one fixed universal bar.

records.summary: Slayer points are both a reroll/consumable resource and a permanent-unlock currency. Assignment streak milestones and Slayer-master access affect point routing.
records.leagueUse: Model master access, streak milestones and League point multipliers as a progression loop; do not import the live-game route as automatically optimal.

records.summary: Non-combat skills feed combat power through prayers, potions, familiars, Slayer unlocks, crafting requirements, Invention, Archaeology relics and Dungeoneering rewards.
records.leagueUse: Show cross-skill dependencies in region/build views so a combat plan can explain which skilling unlocks it needs.

records.summary: PvME's current ability pages reinforce that modern styles have resource generation/consumption, temporary state, target geometry, equipment gates and utility effects that cannot be represented by damage ranges alone.
records.leagueUse: Keep resources, requirements and temporary state as separate fields/hooks so League rules can modify them explicitly.

records.summary: Boss-specific ammo preset pages are not portable League data, but they reveal that ammo choice and ammo effects need their own generic equipment layer.
records.leagueUse: Build a generic ammo/effect catalog after current-source verification; let encounter geometry and region-accessible ammo drive availability instead of importing boss presets.

records.summary: Several PvME page families were crawled but should not be imported wholesale.

details.slayerMonsterGuides: Use only to discover location/access/unique-drop candidates; discard presets and rotations, then verify candidates against the Wiki.
details.bossAndAfkGuides: Exclude rotations, phase instructions, kill rates and presets.
details.combatAchievements: Defer individual requirements until an Equilibrium task explicitly references them.
details.oneTickGuides: Exclude encounter techniques unless a generic timing mechanic is independently verified.

records.leagueUse: Prevents the research corpus from turning into a copied PvME mirror or stale boss-guide database.

records.summary: The PvME website is built from the pvme-guides repository's text guides, which also feed the Discord content.
records.leagueUse: Use the live page URL for attribution when available and the upstream guide file only as a retrieval fallback for flaky routes. The same staleness rules still apply.
